newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan PM's panel calls for more BOJ independence.
newsitem.headline: Japan PM's panel calls for more BOJ independence.

text.p: A key advisory panel on Tuesday proposed giving Japan's central bank more freedom in forming monetary policy, but stopped short of suggesting it be given independence equal to that of central banks in other major nations.

"We have now made the first step to securing the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) independence," Yasuhiko Torii, who heads the eight-member private study panel under Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, told a news conference.
The panel, which has been debating the issue of revising the BOJ law since July, submitted a report to Hashimoto urging an overall revision of the 54-year-old law.

The law stipulates that the status of the BOJ is that it is a body with the aim of steering the economy appropriately under the strong influence of the Finance Ministry. The report said the law was outdated and that the BOJ's aim should be redefined as one of stabilising Japan's prices.

For this purpose, the BOJ should be given more independence and clarify its decision-making process so that it would be able to gain credibility and be effective in the global financial markets, it said.
